newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba mourns death of author Dulce Maria Loynaz.
newsitem.headline: Cuba mourns death of author Dulce Maria Loynaz.

text.p: Poet and novelist Dulce Maria Loynaz, one of Cuba's leading authors, died on Sunday, aged 94, official media reported on Monday.
Her many awards included Spain's prestigious Cervantes literature prize, which she won in 1992.
The official Prensa Latina news agency said in an obituary that Loynaz was born into a well-to-do family in Havana in 1902.
"Her work was distinguished by the faculty of masterfully combining the universal and the Cuban and the use of authenticity in language...," it added.

Loynaz rose to literary prominence in the 1930s and 1940s. Her works included "Jardin", "Obra Lirica" (1955), "Versos" (1920-1938), "Carta de amor al rey tut-ank-kamen" (1953), "Poesias Escogida" (1983), "Bestiarium" (1985) and "Fe de vida", a volume of memoirs published when she was 92.
